outcome: Persistence of hypertension 12 months after delivery
Persistence of hypertension at 3 months from delivery
Persistence of hypertension at 6 months from delivery

Pregnancy complications (earlier onset of pregnancy-related hypertensive disorder, higher dose of nifedipine, receipt of multiple antihypertensive drugs, fetal growth restriction, abnormal Doppler velocimetry, cesarean delivery)
cohort: The study included 124 patients with a history of pregnancy-related hypertensive disorder, comprising 62 with PCOS and 62 age, BMI, and infertility treatment-matched controls without PCOS.
finding: Women with pregnancy-related hypertensive disorder and PCOS had a significantly higher risk of persistent hypertension 12 months after delivery compared to those without PCOS.
mod_finding: The incidence of cesarean delivery was significantly higher in the PCOS group (35.5%) than in the control group (19.4%).
